source_text:
Ἀδελφοί μου, λίαν ἐκκέχυμαι ἀγαπῶν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑπεραγαλλόμενος ἀσφαλίζομαι ὑμᾶς: οὐκ ἐγὼ δέ, ἀλλ’ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, ἐν ᾧ δεδεμένος φοβοῦμαι μᾶλλον, ὡς ἔτι ὢν ἀναπάρτιστος: ἀλλ’ ἡ προσευχὴ ὑμῶν εἰς θεόν με ἀπαρτίσει, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ κλήρῳ ἠλεήθην ἐπιτύχω, προσφυγὼν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ ὡς σαρκὶ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ὡς πρεσβυτερίῳ ἐκκλησίας.
καὶ τοὺς προφήτας δὲ ἀγαπῶμεν, διὰ τὸ καὶ αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον κατηγγελκέναι καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν ἐλπίζειν καὶ αὐτὸν ἀναμένειν, ἐν ᾦ καὶ πιστεύσαντες ἐσώθησαν, ἐν ἑνότητι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὄντες, ἀξιαγαπητοι καὶ ἀξιοθαύμαστοι ἅγιοι, ὑπὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μεμαρτυρημένοι καὶ συνηριθμημένοι ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τῆς κοινῆς ἐλπίδος.
thought_title: The Prophets and Apostles as One Hope in Christ
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Philadelphia while being taken under guard to Rome, and here he speaks of his own incompleteness and the unity of prophets and apostles in the gospel.
pass_a_gloss: My brothers, I am poured out exceedingly loving you and rejoicing greatly I secure you: not I however, but Jesus Christ, in whom being bound I fear rather, as still being incomplete: but the prayer of you to God will complete me, in order that in which lot I was shown mercy I may attain, having fled for refuge to the gospel as to flesh of Jesus, and to the apostles as to council of elders of church, as a typological parallel. And the prophets also we love, because also they into the gospel have announced beforehand and in him hoped and him awaited, in whom also having believed they were saved, in unity of Jesus Christ being, worthy of love and worthy of wonder holy ones, by Jesus Christ having been witnessed to and numbered together in the gospel of the common hope.

choices.why: Keeps the perfect passive force of the verb; Ignatius speaks of himself as wholly expended in love, not merely feeling affection.
The verb means to make firm or safe; the middle voice suggests Ignatius' active concern for their stability.
The word means unfinished or not yet perfected; it fits Ignatius' sense that his martyrdom will complete his discipleship.

choices.english: the lot in which I was shown mercy
choices.why: κλῆρος here is the assigned portion or destiny; the passive of ἐλεέω keeps the divine action in view.

choices.term: προσφυγὼν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ ὡς σαρκὶ Ἰησοῦ
choices.english: having fled for refuge to the gospel as to the flesh of Jesus
choices.why: The gospel is the tangible presence of Christ, parallel to his flesh; the simile must stay explicit.
rejected: taking refuge in the gospel as in Jesus' body
fleeing to the gospel as to Jesus' flesh

choices.why: The perfect participle stresses their established place in the gospel's record of hope.

pass_b_english: My brothers and sisters, I am utterly poured out in love for you, and with overflowing joy I am working to make you secure. Yet it is not I who do this, but Jesus Christ. Because I am still bound in him, I am all the more afraid, since I am still incomplete. But your prayer to God will complete me, so that I may attain the lot in which I was shown mercy. I have taken refuge in the gospel as in the flesh of Jesus, and in the apostles as in the council of elders of the church.

We also love the prophets, because they too announced the gospel beforehand, hoped in him, and waited for him. By believing in him they were saved, being in the unity of Jesus Christ. They are saints worthy of love and worthy of wonder, witnessed to by Jesus Christ and numbered together in the gospel of our common hope.

last_rejected.quote: Because I am still bound in him
last_rejected.why: ἐν ᾧ refers to Jesus Christ, but 'bound in him' misrepresents δεδεμένος (bound/chained as prisoner), not spiritual union.
last_rejected.fix: Because I am still his prisoner, I am all the more afraid
last_rejected.ruling: δεδεμένος means 'bound' (cf. Eph 3:1); 'bound in him' correctly renders ἐν ᾧ δεδεμένος, no meaning change.

last_rejected.why: μεμαρτυρημένοι here means 'attested/approved by Jesus Christ' (bearing witness to their character), not 'witnessed to' which suggests passive reception of testimony.
last_rejected.ruling: μεμαρτυρημένοι = 'witnessed to/borne witness about'; 'witnessed to by' is valid passive rendering, within normal range.

problems.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

problems.why: Reader may think 'council of the apostles' is a historical body separate from 'council of elders', not realizing it's a typological parallel.
problems.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

problems.quote: council of elders of the church
problems.why: Same entity as 'council of elders' elsewhere; 'of the church' adds no distinction but may confuse.

variants.text: council of elders of the church

problems.quote: fled for refuge to the gospel as to the flesh of Jesus
problems.why: Alludes to Hebrews 6:18 (flee for refuge) but not exact; composite allusion.
Same office rendered two ways; readers may think 'elders' are different from 'council of elders.'

edits.old: and to the apostles as to the council of elders of the church.
edits.new: and to the apostles as to the council of elders of the church, as a typological parallel.

fixed: The English already uses 'council of elders' consistently for πρεσβυτέριον; the phrase 'council of elders of the church' is the same entity and does not need standardization.
The allusion to Hebrews 6:18 is not an exact quotation; the English already conveys the same meaning as the source, so no change is needed.

polish.changed: Removed the editorial gloss 'as a typological parallel' and the explanatory phrase 'as a typological parallel' from the first paragraph, and clarified the second paragraph by making 'saints worthy of love and worthy of wonder' a complete sentence referring to the prophets, so the reader can follow the thought without added commentary.

notes.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

notes.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

polish.changed: Clarified the parallel structure of the refuge imagery by using 'in' consistently, and made the subject of each clause explicit so the reader can follow Ignatius's train of thought without stumbling.

notes.quote: I have fled for refuge to the gospel as to the flesh of Jesus
notes.why: 'Fled for refuge' is technical (Greek: kataphyge), but 'as to the flesh of Jesus' is startling; reader may not grasp the parallel structure.
notes.fix: Add note: Ignatius parallels gospel with Christ's flesh and apostles with elders.
